note: A 128-byte stack buffer is allocated to hold DNS record data; kMaxRrDataSize is 128.
A 255-byte name buffer is allocated; OT_DNS_MAX_NAME_SIZE is 255.
The record data buffer size is incorrectly set to sizeof(name) (255) instead of sizeof(data) (128), so the declared capacity exceeds the actual data buffer.
The record data pointer points to the 128-byte stack buffer, but the size field claims 255 bytes.
For each DNS record in the response, the API fills recordInfo with attacker-controlled record data into the 128-byte data buffer.
OutputBytes reads mDataBufferSize (255) bytes from the 128-byte data buffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ past the end of the data array.
The out-of-bounds read is performed here when i exceeds 127, reading beyond the 128-byte stack buffer and triggering the sanitizer.
OutputLine is the caller that formats and emits the record data, reaching the vulnerable OutputBytes read in the crash state.
FinalizeQuery invokes the CLI callback HandleDnsRecordResponse with the parsed DNS response, completing the path from attacker-controlled DNS response to the overflow.
